_comment: The accessory line-up. A SEPARATE manifest from shots.json rather than more items in it, for the reason that file's own header gives: it is the artefact behind the art bake-off, and re-running it has to reproduce the same framings. Run: godot --path . --run-shots art/shots_accessories.json (WINDOWED -- --headless disables rendering).
_lift_comment: EVERY PLAYER IS LIFTED 0.9 m. A player's origin is the MIDDLE of its body and the studio ground is at y = 0, so without the lift the floor cut every character in half at the waist; focus_y is raised by the same amount so the framing is unchanged. The ground is 80 m so the edge of it is never in shot.

studio._comment: THE ANGLES ARE CHOSEN TO MATCH REFERENCE PHOTOGRAPHY, not to flatter the model. Every accessory is rendered from the same five, so a version can be compared against a photograph taken from the equivalent angle AND against the previous version of itself. The subject's own yaw is set so it FACES the camera in each -- a rack judged from behind is a different shape.
studio._backdrop_comment: A SLATE BACKDROP, background and floor both (2026-09-25). The level's sky and pale ground made anything bright vanish -- the tail fire's first render did -- and black smoke reads only against something lighter than itself. Mid-dark and cool, so warm flame, black smoke and every body colour all have contrast against it.

items._comment: THE GAME'S OWN CAMERA. bridge_camera.gd is a fixed 45-degree pitch looking down -Z, so this is the only view that decides whether the thing works in play. Every other shot here is diagnostic; this one is the verdict. The subject faces the camera, which is a player walking TOWARD you.
items.name: moose_game

items._comment: TRUE FRONT. The view field guides use for a moose, because spread and the brow shovels are both square-on to it.
items.name: moose_front

items._comment: TRUE PROFILE. What separates a moose from an elk fastest: an elk's beam sweeps back over the shoulders and a moose's does not. Any back-sweep shows here and nowhere else.
items.name: moose_profile

items._comment: TRUE TOP. Where palmation is unambiguous -- the plate's outline, the bay between brow and main palm, and the fringe of points are all in plan here.
items.name: moose_top

items._comment: AND THE ELK FROM THE SAME FIVE ANGLES. Two racks in one picker are only worth having if a player can tell them apart, and the comparison is worthless unless both are shot identically.
items.name: elk_game

items._comment: The rest of the picker, at the game's angle only -- they are settled, and they are here so a change to the shared machinery cannot break one of them unnoticed.
items.name: acc_none

items._comment: THE SHRIMP TAIL IN FOUR VIEWS: top, side, back and perspective. Tinted dark so the trim colour it wears reads against the studio, and framed back along the tail so the fan and its flame are in shot.
items.name: shrimp_top
